notes: §1985:VI.4.3.2 prints SOURCE-COMPUTER. [ computer-name [ WITH DEBUGGING MODE ] . ]: the second period stands inside the bracket, so it comes only with a computer-name. sourceComputerParagraph parses the superset; VersionConformancePass.VisitDebuggingModeClause admits the clause below 2014 and DebuggingLineRewriter.DeclaresMode compiles the debugging lines; ClosedFormatPass refuses anything else after the name (VisitUnrecognizedClause, COBOL1970) and a name with no closing period (ScreenParagraphPeriods, COBOL3408); and VisitSourceComputerParagraph through GateLonePeriod and ParagraphPeriods.LonePeriod now refuses SOURCE-COMPUTER followed by a lone second period below 2002 (COBOL0900, the landed fix of kb/Work PB5170), the arm the prior read found missing. Probed at --std 85: (b) the empty paragraph and a name alone run (debugging line ignored); a name with the clause, without WITH and across three lines compile the D line; refused are the lone period (accepted at 2002), the clause without a name, DEBUGGING without MODE, the clause twice, two names, a literal name, a period between the name and the clause, a missing header period, a missing closing period, the paragraph twice and after OBJECT-COMPUTER; (c) at 2014 the D line is refused (COBOL0902). The classes of variable-length data, items, files and numeric values do not reach this paragraph. The witness writes XYZ-1 WITH DEBUGGING MODE and shows its debugging line compiled. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5170 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-06.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-06-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "SOURCE-COMPUTER. [ computer-name [ WITH DEBUGGING MODE ] . ]"; 2023: "SOURCE-COMPUTER. [ computer-name-1 ] .". 2023 keeps the paragraph and the optional computer-name, but its format no longer has WITH DEBUGGING MODE, so 1985 programs using that phrase are refused.
